residuals.statement: The b77 review's R-PARAMS (set_params / settable_params / get_params / gettable_params / get_size_ex forwarding a NULL algctx to provider callbacks) is closed at this candidate: all four parameter entry points now test `evp_md_ctx_algctx_is_missing` before the provider call and `EVP_MD_CTX_get_size_ex` refuses (-1) before either callback, and the divergence record and tests were extended.  Not re-measured at runtime here (no build).

57 of the 65 sites have an explicit validity contract only as an operation-level `// SAFETY:` block comment plus the OSSL_FUNC callback ABI; they carry no `# Safety` section on the `unsafe extern "C" fn` interface.  This is the same class the b76 review accepted for its provider-callback sites, and it is not reclassified as a discharge; it is recorded so a future caller audit knows the contract is at the body, not the signature.

b77-review-v1i-repaired.json records `span_sha256_reviewed` for sha3::keccak_final as dd7adaee… (the pre-repair body) while the body it accepted at the repair head hashes to 4dbe9bbd….  The verdict is sound (its `evidence` quotes the repaired body), but the field name does not mean what a reader would assume.  I re-read the body rather than rely on the field.

13 v1i and 6 v1l boundaries that were SAFETY_DISCHARGED in the prior receipts are outside this review's 65-site cohort; none was re-established at this candidate, so the regenerated receipts mark them RETAINED and they cannot discharge.  A further 5 v1i boundaries name items that no longer exist (retired thunks) and are recorded ABSENT.  The remaining 18 v1i and 9 v1l non-cohort boundaries were already non-discharging and keep their original text.  CAMPAIGN-STATUS.json still lists the 19 withdrawn boundaries in scoped_boundary_discharges; that status document was not edited in this batch and must be updated by the orchestrator, or the conflict is detect-only.  No obligation in either b77 closure depended on any of them.

The b78 closure will carry obligations from closure-ssh-b77.json at their old lines (e.g. digest.rs copyctx 658).  The regenerated receipt declares 672.  The receipt's boundaries are also enrolled by the ledger path only where state.json carries a matching obligation_mechanisms record; where they are not, the carried old coordinate remains and must be re-resolved by the closure's current-census-line path.  This is a closure-run property, not a receipt defect, and it is why C9 supplies the resolved line.
No build, test, sanitizer, Miri or timing run was permitted at 12 GiB available (§6.1).  Every verdict is a source-and-static-control verdict.

does_not_prove: It does not establish SAFE_COMPATIBLE for any consumer family; a site receipt is not a family graduation.
It does not establish a boundary-level SAFETY_DISCHARGED for D-DIGEST-NULL-ALGCTX-1 or D-SHA3-FINAL-OUTLEN-1.
It does not prove that the b78 consumer closure discharges anything: the closure was not re-measured here.
It does not prove absence of UB at runtime; no dynamic instrument ran.
It does not establish the NUL-termination of an arbitrary external C caller's ENGINE default-algorithm string.
